title: sodium issue #3013: Texture Bleeding with Custom Models using half pixel translations

text: [issue by MrKinau] ### Bug Description When using a resource pack with models using a custom texture translation, which moves the model by half a pixel, it will result in texture bleeding at the edges. ### Reproduction Steps Steps apply for 1.21.4 only: 1. Install this example resource pack: [test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18725768/test.zip) 2. Select GUI Scale 3 3. Give yourself the test item `/give @s paper[minecraft:item_model="test:test"]` 4. Observe the item has a orange stripe at the left (texture bleeding) ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2be83f4c-3989-4c49-a451-0bcb1ae23418) Additional Info: The resource pack is designed to demonstrate this issue with the following test model: ```json { "parent": "minecraft:item/generated", "textures": { "layer0": "test:custom/test" }, "display": { "gui": { "translation": [0.5, -0.5, 0] } } } ``` Unfortunately the texture bleeding is not visible without changing an additional texture. In my case the atlas generated like this: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1625521a-8f55-4f34-a0ed-ebedba3ecd23) I changed the texture of weeping vines to plain orange and the texture bleeding is visible like seen in the image above. ### Log File [20:01:14] [main/INFO]: Loading Minecraft 1.21.4 with Fabric Loader 0.16.9 [20:01:14] [main/INFO]: Loading 11 mods: - fabricloader 0.16.9 \-- mixinextras 0.4.1 - java 21 - minecraft 1.21.4 - sodium 0.6.6+mc1.21.4 |-- fabric-api-base 0.4.54+b47eab6b04 |-- fabric-block-view-api-v2 1.0.19+7feeb73304 |-- fabric-renderer-api-v1 5.0.2+84404cdd04 |-- fabric-rendering-data-attachment-v1 0.3.57+73761d2e04 |-- fabric-rendering-fluids-v1 3.1.19+7feeb73304 \-- fabric-resource-loader-v0 3.0.11+b1caf1e904 [20:01:14] [main/INFO]: SpongePowered MIXIN Subsystem Version=0.8.7 Source=file:/home//.local/share/PrismLauncher/libraries/net/fabricmc/sponge-mixin/0.15.4+mixin.0.8.7/sponge-mixin-0.15.4+mixin.0.8.7.jar Service=Knot/Fabric Env=CLIENT [20:01:14] [main/INFO]: Compatibility level set to JAVA_21 [20:01:14] [main/INFO]: Loaded configuration file for Sodium: 43 options available, 0 override(s) found [20:01:14] [main/INFO]: Searching for graphics cards... [comment by MrKinau (none)] > but am not any closer to understanding why it is happening It must've been a "more recent" issue as I did not notice it in previous versions. I've just tested which version introduced it and discovered that this issue was not present in sodium 1.21-0.5.11, but is present in sodium 1.21-0.6.0-beta.1-fabric (and I assume every following version). Both versions tested within 1.21 and 1.21.1 [comment by MrKinau (none)] I've just tested every commit individually and could track it down to [this commit](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/commit/ea0172768a5da9907b5a5711160dc3984fafea83) After removing the `FaceBakeryMixin` or in recent versions `TextureAtlasSpriteMixin` I can't reproduce this issue anymore. Actually I have no clue onto what this mixin is for or how to fix this properly, but hopefully me tracking it down helps understanding it a little :) [comment by MrKinau (none)] Is there any proper fix in sight (my method of removing the mixin so far works but surely must have some side effects I just did not realize yet)? Maybe due to item rendering changes in 1.21.6 this could be considered to get fixed? I Would really appreciate it [comment by MrKinau (none)] Unfortunately with Minecraft 1.21.6 this issue is not automagically fixed and still persists (tested with sodium-fabric-0.6.13+mc1.21.6). [comment by MrKinau (none)] Can confirm for 1.21.9 (sodium-fabric-0.7.0+mc1.21.9). Updated repro pack. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Install this example resource pack: [test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22727221/test.zip) 2. Select GUI Scale 3 3. Give yourself the test item `/give @s paper[minecraft:item_model="test:test"]` 4. Observe the item has a orange stripe at the left (texture bleeding) As mentioned above, as a workaround the mixin `core.model.TextureAtlasSpriteMixin` can be removed from the `sodium-common.mixins.json` without any issues (at least I am using Sodium without this mixin for more than half a year without noticing any issues)
